chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
"When you bring the bird into Medina, it is permissible for you to take it out of it as long as you brought it in; and when you bring it into Mecca, it is not permissible for you to take it out."

key_terms.لَيْسَ لَكَ: It is not for you (not permissible)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on bringing birds into Mecca and Medina according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific legal distinction between the sanctity of Medina and Mecca regarding the removal of hunted game, a key detail in the jurisprudence of *Haramayn*. While Medina allows for the entry and subsequent exit of game, Mecca imposes a stricter prohibition on removal, reflecting the unique status of the Kaaba's precinct. This ruling is often discussed alongside the general prohibitions of *Hady* and *Qasr* in Hajj rituals.
